description: Let’s team up and create something awesome
summary: Mission Architect is a browser game where 1–4 players design, launch and operate a complete space mission. Players pick a science goal between spotting wildfires, finding lunar ice, watching solar storms, mapping Mars or seeing the first galaxies then choose an orbit, instruments, spacecraft subsystems, communications and a rocket. Every choice ripples through mass, power, battery, data, delta-v, pointing and budget in real time, so players feel the trade-offs mission teams face. After a design review and team GO/NO-GO poll, the mission flies: players vote on how to handle solar storms, failing reaction wheels, debris alerts and budget cuts. A post-mission report explains why it succeeded or failed and links each choice to real NASA missions. It turns system-level mission design that usually abstract theory  into something students can experiment with in minutes.
details:
What it does. Players work through six design steps (Mission, Orbit, Instruments, Spacecraft, Comms, Launch) then a Design Review. Five scenarios cover Earth, the Moon, Sun–Earth L1, Mars and Sun–Earth L2, plus a sandbox. Three difficulty levels change budget, hazards and hints.

How it works. A simplified engineering model links every decision:

  • Propellant mass from the rocket equation, using each engine's specific impulse and the orbit's delta-v needs (capture burn, yearly station-keeping, end-of-life disposal)
  • Solar arrays sized for end of life, including recharging the battery after each eclipse and weaker sunlight at Mars
  • Battery sized from eclipse length, load and allowed depth of discharge
  • Downlink = radio data rate at that distance × ground-station contact hours, compared with instrument data volume
  • Pointing accuracy, radiation tolerance, thermal control and launcher capacity checks
  • Cost = hardware + 15% integration and test + NASA risk-class premium + launch + yearly operations

The Design Review flags blockers, failures and warnings, each with a plain-language "why it matters". The flight simulation uses launcher reliability, risk class and environment mismatches to drive random faults, and inserts team decision events. Scoring rewards science returned, objectives met, budget reserve, space sustainability and each role's personal goal.

Collaboration. Four roles which were Mission Director, Science Lead, Spacecraft Engineer, Flight Ops & Comms. Each own decisions and a personal goal that pulls against the others (reserve vs. more instruments vs. margins vs. bigger antennas). Everyone must sign GO before launch, and in-flight decisions are a majority vote with the Mission Director breaking ties.

Benefits. No install, no login, works offline on any laptop or phone. Every option carries a short explanation, and a built-in Mission Handbook covers delta-v, eclipses, link budgets, risk classes and debris rules. Design codes let teams share and compare designs.

Tools. HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file, with inline SVG for the spacecraft builder and orbit diagrams. No external libraries.
